bull.b: A 20-year, credit-backed 401 MW lease materially increases long-term contracted revenue visibility and shifts cashflow risk toward a high-credit tenant. This underpins predictable capacity utilization and justifies continued capital deployment into AI/HPC campuses over multiple years.

Approximately $3.0B of cash plus monetization of Abernathy (~$530M sale) provide meaningful runway to fund remaining Lake Mariner capex and initial Muskie build without immediate equity raises, improving funding optionality for multi-year scale-up of data center capacity.

Owning large, power-advantaged sites (Muskie, Morgantown/Chesapeake) with long-term utility arrangements creates structural cost advantage in energy-heavy HPC operations and supports multi-gigawatt expansion, strengthening competitive positioning for future AI/HPC demand.

bear.b: Reported zero shareholders' equity and extreme leverage indicate limited loss-absorbing capacity and constrained financial flexibility. Persistent GAAP deficits could force dilutive financing or restructuring if cash inflows from leases and asset sales slip, raising medium-term solvency risk.

Material negative operating and free cash flow reflect the business is not yet self-funding; continued heavy cash burn pressures the need for external financing or asset sales to fund remaining project capex, potentially increasing funding cost or diluting equity over 2–4 quarters.

Negative adjusted EBITDA and industry-wide electrical labor shortages increase scheduling risk and pre-revenue costs, depressing reported margins until capacity ramps. Persistent execution slippage would delay contracted revenue recognition and raise both operating and financing costs.
